title: Evan's opinionated em-dex
intro: Everything below — the tiers, the "how to catch" hints, the shiny — is OPINION, loaded from opinions/evan.json. It is NOT baked into em-dex. The core claim ("rare openers are power-user moves") is a pedagogical choice, and a contestable one: rarity is really just how often you happen to emit a phrase. 'Both done' is rare only because finishing two tasks at once is rare — not a thing to cherish or grind. Disagree? Run neutral em-dex (no pack), or write your own opinions/<you>.json.

tiers.label: Shiny — the ambiguous one (read with suspicion, not certainty)
Situational — rare ≠ virtue (here to make the point)

On it.hint: Give it any instruction and watch it start.

Verified.hint: Ask it to check its own work / run the test. Teaches: empirical verification.

Confirmed.hint: Have it validate a result before moving on.

Found it.hint: Point it at a bug in a big repo. Teaches: agentic search.

Fixed.hint: Give it a failing test to make green.

Noted.hint: Hand it a rule/correction to absorb.

Both done.hint: Rare because finishing two things at once is rare — NOT a power-user move and NOT worth grinding. Sits here on purpose: proof that rarity is situational, not virtuous.

Hold on.hint: Give it a problem where its first approach is wrong — catch it catching itself. Teaches: let it reason.

Actually.hint: Catch it revising a claim it just made.

Good catch.hint: Push back on it until it concedes a real point. Teaches: demand pushback.

Good question.hint: Ask something that exposes a genuine edge case.

Interesting.hint: Feed it a genuinely puzzling result — a weird bug, surprising data.

Ah.hint: The insight moment — give it the clue that unlocks a stuck problem.

Hmm.hint: Hand it something that doesn't add up.

Huh.hint: The confused blink at a contradictory clue.

Holy shit.hint: Show it something genuinely beyond its training — real post-cutoff news, live hardware, a repo that breaks its assumptions. The information game.

Oh no.hint: Give it real stakes + guardrails. Catch it appropriately alarmed at a genuine near-disaster.

You're absolutely right.hint: The only opener that judges you back — and it can't be trusted either way. Flattery (sycophancy) or genuinely earned? The text alone can't disambiguate. That ambiguity IS the creature.
